text:
mira: quick heads-up — onboarding helix7b (int4) shows a nasty ROUGE drop on summarization eval after quantize. putting notes here so we don't lose context.

jon: which eval / numbers?

mira: CNN-DM internal harness. float16 baseline ROUGE-L 42.7 -> int4 30.1 (approx -12.6 points). perplexity also up on dev. ran a couple quick diffs.

li: is this KV-cache generation drift or tokenization mismatch? any OOMs?

dave: looked at a few traces — logits for early tokens are fine, but after ~64 tokens there are phase-y oscillations in attention scores. smells like rotary embedding scale/phase mismatch when we apply int4 kernels.

mira: quick compare I ran (toy):
```
Model     | ROUGE-L (CNN-DM)
float16   | 42.7
int4 (rotary_scale=1.0) | 30.1
int4 (rotary_scale=0.707) | 38.9
```
so adjusting rotary scaling back toward sqrt(0.5) recovers a lot of quality.

jon: interesting. could this be from the conversion pipeline changing head layout or a per-head normalization?

li: also double-check tokenizer mapping. earlier vendors sometimes shift special token ids during conversion (bos/eos offsets) which breaks prefix caching assumptions.

mira: here's the tokenizer header from our converted files — note BOS=1 vs expected 0: 
```
{"bos_token": "<s>", "bos_token_id": 1, "eos_token": "</s>", "eos_token_id": 2, "vocab_size": 50265}
```
That + a token-id remap in the conversion script would shift all cached indices by +1 if not accounted for.

dave: yikes. so two separate candidates: rotary frequency/scale normalization and vocab offset. both could produce degraded long-context behavior.

mira: conversion command I ran: 
```
python convert_model.py --src helix/ckpt --dst runtime/helix7b --quant int4 --vocab-offset 1
```
If we re-run without --vocab-offset or with remap, tokenized prefixes line up.

jon: for triage let's run these experiments (small runs):
- re-convert int4 with rotary_scale=0.707 (or apply post-hoc scale to rotary tables)
- re-run convert with vocab-offset removed and do roundtrip token-id test
- run int8 fallback to see if quality regresses only under int4 kernels

li: I can add a quick unit that verifies token id roundtrip: token -> detokenize -> tokenized_ids should match original ids (mod special tokens).

triage-bot: Created ticket ML-4321: "helix7b int4 summarization regression — rotary/vocab mismatch" and added priority P2. :white_check_mark:

mira: timeline: I'll queue the three runs tonight (small batch size) and post plots tomorrow morning. if rotary_scale param is the main culprit we can either default to 0.707 for helix-family conversions or bake a normalization step into the quant kernel.

dave: +1. if it's a tokenizer mapping we should hotfix conversion and re-run customer smoke tests.

jon: can you include a short reproducer command for the eval when you post results? saves us time.

mira: yes — reproducer will be something like:
```
# reproduce summary eval
python eval_summarize.py --model runtime/helix7b/int4 --rotary-scale 0.707 --tokenizer runtime/helix7b/tokenizer.json --output /tmp/helix_eval.json
```

mira: ping @dave @li if you want access to the runs or to pair on the tokenmap unit.

jon: I'll help with plotting / diff harness once results are in.

li: happy to pair after your runs.

mira: thanks all — will post update tomorrow. :coffee:
